newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Construction positive about H1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Construction positive about H1 '97.

text.p: Volvo Construction Equipment (VCE), a unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, said on Wednesday it ended 1996 on a strong note in North America and forecast a positive first half to 1997 in the area.
"We thought a while ago that (the market in) North America would fall this year," Michel Mudler, senior vice president at VCE, told an analyst meeting in Stockholm.
"We do not think so anymore. At least the first half of the year should be as strong as 1996. The other half year might not be as strong."
The construction vehicles company has 23 percent of the total sales in that market in North America.
Although Mudler said the company did well in North America at the end of 1996, he refrained from giving any details barely a month ahead of Volvo's annual report.
Regarding Germany, where VCE has almost 20 percent of total sales, Mudler was not so optimistic.
"Germany keeps looking weak after too large purchasing orders during the early nineties," he said. "Other European countries are stronger, but because of Germany, Europe looks weaker this year."
Including Germany, VCE has 60 percent of sales in Europe.
Elsewhere, Mudler said the South East Asia market is likely to keep growing by two-digit figures and that the Latin America market finally seems to take off and grow this year.
